items.prompt: A UTF-8 CSV starts with field names and contains empty and repeated customer_id values. With header=true and customer_id required, how should version 1.0 handle invalid keys?

options.A: Reject empty keys and duplicate keys; retain valid rows.
options.B: Generate new IDs for empty keys; reject duplicate keys.
options.C: Reject empty keys; keep duplicates when other fields differ.
options.D: Skip empty keys silently; keep the last duplicate row.

items.rationale: A follows I1. B invents ID generation, C allows prohibited duplicates, and D invents silent skipping and duplicate resolution.
items.cognitive_level: Apply/analyze documented rules within a scenario
items.intended_challenge: Distinguish adequate evidence from plausible shortcuts; empirical difficulty unknown
items.author: AI draft, fictional Northstar case

items.prompt: Of 1,000 rows, 970 are accepted, 20 rejected for empty keys and 10 for duplicate keys. No exclusion is agreed. What should the consultant recommend?

options.A: Publish the 970 rows and record the rejection counts as the disposition.
options.B: Retry the original input and compare the next rejection report before deciding.
options.C: Resolve rejected rows through documented correction or an explicitly agreed exclusion.
options.D: Ask the customer to verify the 970 accepted rows before publishing that subset.

items.rationale: C follows I2. A/D leave rejected rows without an agreed disposition; B retries unchanged invalid input without resolving it.

items.intended_challenge: Distinguish adequate evidence from plausible shortcuts; empirical difficulty unknown
items.author: AI draft, fictional Northstar case

items.prompt: A 1,000-row import reports 990 accepted and 5 rejected. The five-row gap has no explanation. Which next step follows the documented reconciliation procedure?

options.A: Record the gap as duplicate suppression and continue to value verification.
options.B: Investigate the gap and escalate it to the data owner if unresolved.
options.C: Apply a 99 percent acceptance threshold and continue to value verification.
options.D: Inspect five accepted rows and use their values to close the accounting gap.

items.rationale: B follows I2/I3. A invents a disposition; C invents a threshold; D confuses sampling with accounting.

items.prompt: Counts reconcile and rejection dispositions are documented. Required mappings and representative values still need verification, and release evidence must be retained. What role can preview --limit 5 play?

options.A: Repair mapping errors in the displayed rows before the full release check.
options.B: Validate every accepted row by checking five representative returned values.
options.C: Replace the mapping check once five returned rows match the source values.
options.D: Inspect returned accepted rows without changing their values or mappings.

items.rationale: D follows I3. Preview is non-mutating and limited; A invents repair, B generalizes to all rows, and C omits the separate mapping check.

items.prompt: Complete an ingestion evidence sheet and publication recommendation for B-17.
items.setup: Synthetic paper case; no commands executed. Previous published P-16 remains available. UTF-8 CSV header customer_id,amount. Six data rows: 1 C101,10; 2 C102,20; 3 [empty],30; 4 C102,40; 5 C105,50; 6 C106,60. Supplied rejection report: row 3 empty key and row 4 duplicate key. Accepted=4, rejected=2. Configuration: header=true, customer_id required. Preview shows C101/10 and C105/50. Mapping log maps source amount to destination customer_name instead of amount. No exclusion agreed. Treat the report as authoritative about which duplicate row was rejected; do not invent duplicate semantics.
items.deliverable: One sheet with configuration/mapping findings, row accounting, rejection disposition/rerun plan and publication recommendation with evidence and escalation. Distinguish supplied evidence from proposed repairs.

rubric.anchor: 2: identifies appropriate header/key settings AND wrong amount mapping requiring correction; 1: only one; 0: neither or accepts mapping.
2: gives 4+2=6 and says count agreement alone does not authorize release; 1: correct arithmetic without release implication; 0: arithmetic wrong or says totals alone permit release.

2: addresses both invalid keys through correction with owner input or explicit agreed exclusion, then rerun/reconcile; 1: fully handles one or omits agreement/rerun; 0: silent exclusion or unchanged retry as repair.

2: holds pending corrected mapping/dispositions and representative recheck, retains source/reconciliation and previous version, escalates unresolved discrepancy to data owner; 1: holds with incomplete evidence/rechecks/escalation; 0: recommends publication now.

items.rationale: Evidence-sheet exercise integrates documented checks and action planning; it does not observe software execution.

items.prompt: Under Northstar 2.0, an integration must read only orders. Which complete grant plan meets the requirement?

options.A: Assign workspace traverse; leave dataset grants empty.
options.B: Assign dataset orders query; leave workspace grants empty.
options.C: Assign workspace traverse; assign dataset orders query.
options.D: Assign workspace reader; leave dataset grants empty.

items.rationale: C follows A1: traverse and dataset query are jointly required. A lacks query, B lacks traversal, and D grants access beyond orders.

items.prompt: The orders service account must read orders, be unable to write orders, and be unable to read unrelated customer data. Which verification record establishes all three requirements?

options.A: Administrator: orders read succeeds, orders write denied, unrelated read denied.
options.B: Service account: orders read succeeds, orders write denied, unrelated read denied.

options.D: Service account: orders read succeeds, orders write untested, unrelated read denied.

items.rationale: B tests every requirement under the intended identity (A2). A uses the wrong identity; C/D omit a required negative test.

items.prompt: A service token was disclosed in a shared note. The incident record contains no secret. Which response follows the documented procedure?

options.A: Revoke the disclosed token and obtain an authorized replacement.
options.B: Rename the service account and continue using its current token.
options.C: Issue a replacement token and leave the disclosed token active.
options.D: Remove the shared note and keep the token until scheduled rotation.

items.rationale: A follows A3. B/C/D leave the disclosed credential valid; note deletion does not revoke it.

items.prompt: For Northstar 2.0, complete an access evidence sheet for svc-orders and a safe remediation sequence.
items.setup: Synthetic 2.0 paper case; no token supplied or changes executed. Requirement: read orders only. Current grant: workspace reader. A proposed replacement has workspace traverse only and no dataset query grant. Under the CURRENT broad grant, svc-orders orders read succeeds, orders write is denied, unrelated customer ledger read succeeds. An administrator read also succeeds. No tests of the proposed replacement have run. A service token was disclosed in a shared note, represented only as TOKEN_REDACTED.
items.deliverable: One sheet: exact grant replacement and explanation of each required component; interpretation of current results and proposed replacement; service-identity recheck plan; token response sequence; credential-free incident/evidence record. Separate proposed actions from supplied observations.

rubric.anchor: 1: removes workspace reader and specifies both workspace traverse and dataset orders query. 0: any required change missing, or endorses broad access or either grant alone.
1: explains that traverse alone cannot read data and query alone cannot navigate the workspace. 0: either explanation missing or contradicted.

2: identifies current ledger success as failure and requires service-identity orders read success, orders write denial and unrelated-data denial after BOTH replacement grants; 1: recognizes exposure but rechecks incomplete; 0: accepts administrator test or current results as verification of proposed replacement.
2: revokes disclosed token and gets authorized replacement; 1: only one; 0: rename/add token only or keep using disclosed token.

2: records identity, outcomes and incident/action status without secrets and labels proposed rechecks as proposed; 1: safe record with missing identity/status detail; 0: copies secret or falsely claims remediation happened.

items.rationale: 2.0 A1 changes remediation to two jointly necessary grants. A2 verification and A3 revocation/replacement remain required. Paper evidence planning does not demonstrate actual execution.

source_refs.locator: A1 Grant; A2 Verify; A3 Compromise

items.prompt: A snapshot is two hours old and no recovery objective is recorded. Which rehearsal plan follows the documented procedure?

options.A: Restore over active data; request customer confirmation of acceptable age.
options.B: Restore separately; apply a one-day age limit from the team template.
options.C: Restore separately; let the consultant set the acceptable-loss objective.
options.D: Restore separately; seek the missing customer-approved recovery objective.

items.rationale: D follows R1. A risks active data; B/C substitute an unapproved objective. Acceptable loss cannot be claimed until the customer objective is known.

items.prompt: A separate restore passes verification and meets the approved recovery objective. A cutover/rollback recommendation is ready and the old namespace is retained. Which authorization sequence permits redirecting clients?

options.A: Record the consultant's approval of this version, then redirect clients.
options.B: Record the customer's approval of this version, then redirect clients.
options.C: Redirect clients after the checks, then request the customer's approval.
options.D: Use the customer's approval of an earlier version, then redirect clients.

items.rationale: B follows R3. A substitutes consultant authority, C reverses authorization order, and D does not authorize the exact version.

items.prompt: Complete a recovery evidence sheet and recommendation for R-22.
items.setup: Synthetic paper case, no executable lab. Active prod-old remains in service. Immutable S-22 snapshot taken 08:00; decision time 11:00. Customer-approved maximum snapshot age is four hours. Separate restore target rehearsal-new. Manifest count=500; restored=497. Representative IDs/values match supplied manifest examples. Intended service identity reads orders, is denied orders write, but CAN read unrelated customer data. Job status complete. No customer cutover authorization.
items.deliverable: One sheet: age/namespace checks, count/value/permission findings, hold/cutover decision and investigation plan, conditional cutover/rollback and authorization record. Separate observed evidence from required rechecks.

rubric.anchor: 2: computes three-hour age within four-hour objective AND confirms separate namespace protects active data; 1: only one; 0: wrong age or proposes overwrite.
2: identifies three-row mismatch AND excess service access despite completion/sample match; 1: one failure; 0: accepts restore as verified.
2: holds cutover for investigation/correction and repeat counts/values/intended-permission tests; 1: holds with incomplete follow-up; 0: cutover despite a failure.

2: retains prod-old, specifies rollback route to retained namespace and requires customer authorization with actor/exact version before redirect; 1: retains old and requires approval but lacks rollback/version detail; 0: deletes old, redirects unapproved or claims incident command.

items.rationale: Evidence-sheet exercise integrates documented checks and action planning; it does not observe software execution.

public.overview: Fictional product 2.0 development draft for bounded implementation reasoning. No credential launch or passing rule is approved; the historical 1.0 pilot is synthetic.
public.audience: Partner implementers; excludes architecture, incident command and commercial management.
public.eligibility: Proposed volunteers with implementation exposure; owner confirmation pending.
public.format: Proposed 12 tasks: nine selected-response questions and three written evidence-sheet practicals; 70 minutes unvalidated. Existing LMS and evidence sheets. These do not observe actual software execution.
public.permitted_resources: Proposed: supplied product 2.0 access reference, unchanged ingestion/recovery procedures and personal notes; individual work without outside or generative assistance. Owner confirmation pending.
public.accommodations: Contact Morgan privately before scheduling; final process/contact route pending.
public.retakes: No pass/fail or awards in pilot; future policy pending.
public.appeals: Raise concerns privately to Morgan; deadline and independent reviewer pending.
public.support: Morgan Lee (fictional); contact channel and registration pending.
